correctness.rationale: For each even L>=4, F=OE is a product of two involutions. F^2 x=x iff OE x=EO x, equivalent at each site to one explicit five-bit commutation predicate. Its exhaustive truth table forbids exactly six words, and the 16-state de Bruijn closed-walk trace enumerates all length-L cyclic strings with no such windows. F-fixed points split into independent cyclic length-L/2 words with no adjacent zeros, giving Lucas-square. Subtraction and division by two give exact prime-two orbits. Exact integer Faddeev–LeVerrier coefficients reproduce the polynomial and the reciprocal cubic proves the unique dominant root. A standalone pure-Python checker independently exhausts all 2^L inputs for even L=4..16.

originality.rationale: This is an exact full-configuration-space prime-two-cycle census for the fixed staggered Rule 201 Floquet map. Inspected same-rule full primary texts establish integrability and local correlations but do not provide this count. Especially, the 2008 Lucas/Fibonacci *dynamics-group orbit* factorization acts with arbitrary local update words and is not a prime-two-cycle classification for this specific ordered product. Source and alternative-statement searches found no equivalent or stronger formula; listed residual risks bound this best-knowledge judgment.
residual_risks: A different order-specific cycle calculation for Rule 201 might exist in papers not located by semantic and exact web searches.
The 2008 all-local-update dynamics group permits more elaborate inference if supplemented with new order-specific permutation information, but no implication was found in its stated theorems.
Finite brute-force data alone does not justify novelty or all-size validity; both require the included proof and source comparison.

value.rationale: A natural complete classification of the smallest nonfixed recurrent components of a standard integrable Floquet lattice automaton, uniformly for every even volume and unrestricted bitstrings, not an arbitrary finite slice. The explicit six-pattern subshift, transfer polynomial and algebraic entropy distinguish prime-two orbit growth from fixed-point Lucas growth. This provides exact two-state Floquet permutation blocks and a reusable combinatorial description of their support, structurally complementing previous influence-matrix and group-orbit research.
